On the table are six coloured hats corresponding to the colour of the friends and each friend has to sit at the right coloured hat. Orm sits at the bottom left of the screen so there is a space at the table and here you can move the friends into the correct position. Each friend is highlighted one at a time for a few seconds and when the friend you want to move is highlighted then a press of a key moves him there.

171417.overview:
Orm and Cheep: Narrow Squeaks is a game based on the British children's puppet TV show from the 80s on CITV, where the two main characters are friends, Orm (Worm) and Cheep (Bird). The game is split into four mini-games with the first three single-screen side-view games and the last one is a vertically-scrolling game where the screen scrolls upwards constantly viewed from an elevated angle. Before you start the game you have to play a Reaction test to find out the difficulty of the game. The words Orm and Cheep are at the start of the screen and move down one at a time. You have to stop each word as close to a line by pressing a key. After each game has been played you are giving a score by removing squares from a picture and the better your score, the more of the picture you see. The four games are played with the keyboard with just one key press to play and the games are:

Cheep's Game: Orm is having a lie-in in bed and so Cheep has decided to help put the dishes away by picking them up and placing them on top of each other. Some cups are sitting in the bottom left of the screen and the next dish, which is a saucepan appears on the screen. Cheep moves around the screen constantly in one direction and pressing a key changes his direction by 90 degrees. You must keep changing direction to position Cheep above the dish before you keep changing his direction again to place it on top of the other dishes. if you hit the sides of the screen or another dish then the dish disappears and you have to get it again. Once all the dishes have been stacked then they collapse and Orm is woken up

Crow's Game: Now awake, Orm decides to go for a morning stroll but Crow has spotted Orm and trapped him behind a tree. Cheep, Mouse, Snail and Mole have come to the rescue and the way to get rid of Crow is to dance in front of him. You watch a sequence of the animals dancing one at a time before you keep watching the same sequence. When you notice a wrong part of the sequence you press a key and this moves Crow a small distance up the screen. Each time Crow moves up the screen then you watch a new sequence and Orm is safe when Crow has moved off the screen.

Rat's Game: Orm is safe but Cheep, Snail and Mouse are now trapped by Rat in a hollow tree trunk with Rat guarding the exit in the top right corner. Hedgehog has appeared and will try to get his friends out of the trunk one at a time, by protecting them with his spikes from the bottom left of the screen. Each animal takes it in turns to flash and pressing a key now has that animal moving around the other animal in 90 degree turns. Once you are happy with their position, pressing a key makes both animals flash one at a time again. While you are moving, Rat moves one place at a time around the screen and if he touches Hedgehog's friend then both move back to the bottom left of the screen.

Orm's Game: After the morning excitement, Orm is exhausted and so has decided to go to bed.

171418.overview: Othello is based on the board game where each player attempts to have more counters on the board than their opponent on a 8 x 8 grid. The game starts with both players having two counters in the center of the board diagonal from each other. To take another piece, the player places a counter to have a number of their opponents counters between two of the players counters, vertical, horizontal or diagonal. The opponents color is then turned into the players color and it is then the other players turn. This carries on until the board is full or no counters can be placed.

171427.overview: Othello, also called Reversi, is a strategic board game played by two parties on a grid, usually 8x8 but this one is 6x6. The game uses pieces with a white and a dark face, representing the two players' colors. Players lay pieces on the board alternately, one stone at a time. Every piece has to be put at a place where it touches the opponent's stone row of any length, while there is a player's stone at the of the row. All captured stones in between can then be reversed and become the player's color. The only limitation is that the entire row needs to be of a single color and without free spaces. When all pieces are used, the players with more pieces of his color on the board is the winner. This version is intended to be controlled with lightpen technology.

171428.overview: Out on a Limb is a flick screen platform game based on the fairy tale Jack and the Beanstalk. You play as Jack (the C64 version has you resembling a famous plumber) who must climb the beanstalk, jump over clouds and explore the Giant's castle looking for a golden harp, golden egg and a bag of gold. There are 23 screens to be explored. As you move about the screen jumping over various platforms you have to be careful not to touch any of the creatures that move about the screens as this will lose one of four lives. Scattered around the castle are other treasures to collect as well and your score is based on how long you spend in each room and how long your game was.

171430.overview: Can Alex color all the cubes without getting bonked by the gumdrops? Will he be vaporized by Grody the Witch or bit by Buzzbat? Watch out, Eraser Rabbit is stealing your colors, and Croak the Frog is smashing your cubes! Escape on a cloud...and melt Grody with rain. Then zap Buzzbat with a bolt of lightning.

172128.overview:
Today is August 27th, 1904. Nine months ago, you, Emilia Vittorini, joined the Italian Archeological Expedition in Egypt led by Ernesto Schiaparelli, the director of the Egyptian Museum of Turin. You are now back in Genova, Italy: your steam ferry arrived three days ago with 25 wooden boxes containing Queen Nefertari Meritmut's grave goods, a real treasure! They left Genova by train, heading towards Turin, yesterday evening. While they were in transit, you were invited to a sumptuous reception organised by a wealthy art lover, Eugenio Collovati, count of Raligotto, but it would be hard to say that you appreciated the evening.

But the reception was yesterday: now, you must catch the train to Turin and check that the treasure arrived safely. I will be your eyes and ears. Good luck.

173031.overview:
A Shoot'em Up - SEUCK based vertical space battle game. It seems that all is now lost on the distant planet Deimos, the Rutilians have managed to reach the interplanetary base where the access and defense codes are kept. Nothing can be done to arrest them. But a scientist from the super-confederacy has created a new Nova-Proton weapon, a new experimental ship that autonomously governed, therefore free from computer ties, could be able to infiltrate the enemy defense network, fight their cruisers and fighters, destroy their missile bases and turn the tables. But for such a high tech ship, a special and highly skilled pilot is also required. You as a member of Odin, have been chosen to lead this Nova Force on this difficult mission, to restore peace and tranquility to Deimos, but also to save all humanity from a huge disaster. 

Published in Italy as Odino in Special Program n.46 (settembre 1988) and later in Hit Parade C64 n.30 (Gennaio 1989).

173087.overview: The Oakflat Nuclear Power Plant Simulator is a single player, shareware, simulation of the operation of a nuclear power station. The object of the game is to maintain a stable reaction and generate electricity by manipulation of the control rods and the primary & secondary cooling pumps. After each attempt the player is given a score based on how much power was generated and how long the reactor was running. The simulation has been in existence for many years and on three different platforms. Over time it has matured and increased in complexity to include among other things earthquake and other disaster simulations, and extensive controls, self test functions, and improved sounds. The current Windows release is designed to simulate a 1.5 GWe pressurized light-water nuclear reactor and adjoining power plant. It is operated by either the keyboard or a mouse or both to control rod settings, coolant pump rates, damage control, pressure release valves, reactor scrams, and much more and it maintains a log file so that the player can review the impact of their actions/inaction and make better decisions next time.

173088.overview: Not bad for a minimalist adventure. The sign says, "Beware the Tomb of Shalimar", but you're an adventurer, right? See if you can make your way through it and find the treasures it hides.

173089.overview: Released as part of "Arcade Action" and "Action Thrillers" game pack

173090.overview: You are standing in the main foyer of the starship ZEUS 11. Explore the ship and finish the Oddessy.

173094.overview: A Viking themed text adventure written by Elise C. Bucher aka Zosia the Pious. The game was uploaded to Q-Link in 1986, according to the 1988 Public Domain QLink Software Catalogue. Pray at the various altars for random help messages, when you are hungry just eat food. In the end you need to rescue Sif.

173106.overview: A one or two player single-screen platformer created by The Wizards and published by Logo Software in 1992.

173107.overview: Ograton is an arcade collect 'em up game where your goal is to guide a bouncing ball through a maze, collecting treasures and avoiding obstacles. Your ball moves back and forth on wires until you release it, at which point it bounces around the maze until it hits another wire. It has a limited number of "hit points" so you must time your releases to steer the ball over treasures while avoiding laser cannons and evil black "zombie" balls. Once you have obtained the correct numbers and types of treasures, an exit opens which takes you to the next of the 20 mazes. Published in Game On 1993/09.

173108.overview: An arcade - collect'em up style game created by Nick Peck & Kinley of Fresh Productions and released by CP Verlag in 1995.

173134.overview: Published in 64 Tape Computing No. 07 (1985/xx). You start near the edge of a large forest, the object of the game is to clear the forest of as many trees and rocks as possible without damaging the mills. Don't let the Ogre catch you.

173135.overview: Published in 64'er Sonderheft 54, the arcade style collect'em'up game challenges you to explore for oil with your drilling rig without hitting an enemy in much the same way that the more popular Oil's Well game did.

173136.overview: Is it an Easy peasy Anteater/Aardvark clone or it it an Oil's Well clone? Created by Bluestone (Budget) Productions and published in Golden Disk 64 1991/07. Are you smart enough to be at least as successful as J.R.? Or do you prefer to trust your own nose when it comes to the oil business? There are many dangers in oil production; Above all, make sure you get to the destination quickly and safely.

173138.overview: A casino gambling game published by Cascade Games and also in Digital Marketing PD #234

173139.overview: Oldbones is a board/strategy game that was published by Cascade Game in their rather infamous Cassette 50 compilation.

173140.overview:
Prepare for combat action in this horizontally scrolling space shooter published in both 64'er Sonderheft 37 and Digital Marketing PD #163. The game "Omega Force One" is a technically perfect program from the genre of "Shoot'em Up" games, in which the aim is to destroy the aliens attacking in constantly new formations with your own spaceship and yourself not to be hit: Live and let die.

The game idea has certainly often been declared dead, complex games such as role-playing games or action-adventures seemed to supplant the simple concept, but despite all this, these lone fighters in action against foreign powers are not dying out. The version presented here by one of our readers from Denmark prepares the idea with perfectly animated and beautifully drawn sprites as well as good sound effects and melodies.

173165.overview: A game, precursor to Omega Race with paddle controller support.

173166.overview:
The original Omega Race was modified in 1987 to include modern character sets, new sprites and high resolution pictures and selectable speeds to the game. 

Like the original, you control a spaceship and shoot down the enemy "Droid" ships that attack you. Your ship must survive Droid-dropped mines too--but you can shoot them too. The last ship of the Droid flights goes into a spiraling pattern.

There is no end to this game. Rather, it is a game in which you try to get the highest score, or complete the highest number of levels.

You control a small triangle that is your ship. The ship can turn, move forward (with thrusters) and fire. Movement is one of the games challenges; once the ship is moving, it can only be slowed by turning the nose in the opposite direction and use the thrusters. While doing that, the ship is unable to fire toward anything it is in motion toward.

Bouncing also comes into play during movement. When the ship hits the side of the screen, a wall of force appears, and the ship bounces. You don't have control over where the ship bounces, and must take time to regain control, before you run into an enemy ship and die.

173167.overview:
A mix between space invaders, a wave shooter with the added cross-hairs element that increases the difficulty somewhat. Destroy the space invaders before they reduce your spaceship to a fistful of cosmic dust. They line up in combat order according to their ranks. They dive towards you trying to hit you and then com back up to prepare for a new attack. Keep your eyes peeled, as their movements are unpredictable and this makes them extremely dangerous. If you manage to destroy the entire fleet, a new wave of increasingly fierce aliens will appear to harass you again. 

Published in Italy as Cannone Laser in Commodorissimo - versione tedesca and Game 2000 n.9 (dicembre 1985).

173168.overview: A shoot'em up published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1987/04 (Issue #46), COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1988 Special Issue. Be ready and alert. A host of deadly enemies can make quick work of you in this frantically paced, multilevel arcade-action game for the 64. A joystick is required. "Omicron" is a game which creates a universe full of hostile aliens. To play and win, you must survive 16 waves of 15 enemies each. This is anything but an easy task — you'll be facing some of the deadliest and fastest creatures ever to visit the screen of your computer,

173169.overview: A brain\logic game created by Axel Scheuer and published in 64'er Sonderheft 85.

173182.overview: It is a fruit\slot machine. You can work out your need to feed coins without the expense or travel! High resolution graphics make this the ultimate video slot machine game. Just pull the handle and watch the fruit spin. The computer will keep track of your winnings. Good luck!

173189.overview: Inspired by Operation Wolf, this is a military cross-hairs shooter.

173190.overview: Quite a nice and polished fighting game from 1987, featuring some ripped Rob Hubbard music for good measure. You can kick enemies, or shoot them with a gun or bazooka, or throw grenades at them. There doesn’t seem to be too much to do apart from that and go between two floors at present. It is a nice show case of a game that had some potential.

173191.overview: Taking on the role of special agent Robert "Rip" Steel, it is up to you to destroy the evil Yellow Shadow's network of undersea mining bases. At the same time, you must protect your own bases from attack. You are in command of a small but powerful submarine, and must work quickly and strategically, if you are to succeed.

173192.overview: Operation Proboszcz is a first person shooter. The game takes place on a single screen location. The player's task is to track down and kill all the priests. A new priest appears every few seconds in a various window of the church. The player moves viewfinder to the right, left, up or down and performs shoot. The game offers two difficulty levels - for standard players and radical Catholics. The second one causes viewfinder to move in unpredictable ways, as if the player was drunk.

173193.overview: An Arcade 2D, spy-themed adventure game where two player mode is available via modem. Enter into a world of fast-action and espionage as you search the mysterious Antimatter Complex for top secret documents.

173194.overview: The aliens from the distant planet Zekloke have established a large military complex on Mars which presents a great threat to Earth. Your job is to sneak into the alien complex and destroy it, but you must also find the plans for a powerful defense shield which are known to be hidden in the complex.

173195.overview:
Published in Magic Disk 64 1991/06, and created by  Joachim von Haacke and Michael Kukat, this simultaneous 2 player game is a Snake/Worm variant.
 
OPIUM - In this game, the uninitiated observer is immediately struck by the unusual name. Should this game have an intoxicating effect, a kind of dope on disk? Do you get addicted to it or is it forbidden to use it? Many unanswered questions that prompted the Magic Disc team to start a large-scale awareness campaign - in the form of this game test.

First of all, I can reassure you; OPIUM on the MD is completely harmless in every respect and in no way endangers the life and limb of our users.
With OPIUM, Joachim von Haacke, Michael Kukat and Stefan Harwig from Heaven Artworks have created an entertaining pastime for two players competing against each other. With OPIUM there is a choice between two different background graphics, which are prompted at the start of the game. Paradoxically, the display for both players at the bottom of the screen is exactly the wrong way round.

The principle of OPIUM is as follows:

When a player moves his "dot" away from the wall, the spots on which the dot sits will glow for a number of game movements. The player's point thus receives a kind of tail and soon looks like a snake. However, he is not allowed to touch the wall or the background or his opponent with his snake. Touching oneself by walking back is also not allowed. If a player violates these principles, he has one less round, his score increases by one point and his opponent receives this point - a so-called Carnap - in the final scoring. The only exception to this principle is the diagonal crossing of both "player lines" on both sides, nothing happens here and the game continues without incident. As you have probably already noticed, the whole thing boils down to encircling the enemy by skilfully manoeuvring his snake and leaving him no other option than to touch the wall, the background, himself or you. This would then be a point - or Carnap - for you. Generally speaking, the longer you play, your queues get longer, longer and longer. . 
This also increases the risk of carelessly "biting your own tail" and losing it in this way. The winner is the player who has the most Carnaps in his account at the end of all rounds.

173196.overview: A puzzle game created by Axel Teichmann and published in both Game On 1992/01, and in Abo Disk #3. In this one you are a frog and must use your hopping skills and the blank island to manipulate all matches together without stranding yourself.

173198.overview:
A tile matching puzzle game created by  Art Project Studios, and  published in  Magic Disk 64 1994/08. 

In this puzzle game you have to try to clear all stones from the screen. 99 seconds are given to the player for each level. The aim of the game is to always match the colored stones with those that look the same. Then the arrow-shaped figure must jump from the connected stones to one of the different-looking stones that are also connected to the stones. This is how the connected stones dissolve. But sometimes you have to be darned careful, because some stones are not in pairs either, because they are three times in the playing field. Now you have to try to bring all three into contact at the same time. One type of stone always remains at the end, the so-called joker stone. If there are several on the screen, it is advisable not to connect all of them, but to use them for all purposes.

Some stones only serve as an obstacle to make things a little more difficult. Speaking of difficult! All of this sounds pretty complicated and boring, but it isn't, but you will find that out very quickly in a short test game. Use the joystick in port # 2 to move the arrow in all directions (attention! The figure can only move on stones!). If the fire button is held down, the stone on which the figure is currently located is moved. "" restarts the level if you have manoeuvred yourself into a completely hopeless situation (three times possible!).

173199.overview: The idea of the game is to clear each screen by pushing blocks to match up a minimum of two or more squares. The game has three difficulty settings and an unlockable fourth setting that can be accessed once you have mastered 'hard' mode. ORACLE III features 32 levels on each difficulty setting - making a total of 128 levels for you to solve! The game is very nicely presented with a good selection of options - including difficulty settings, the option to toggle in-game music + sfx, the option to remove the level backgrounds leaving only the puzzle blocks on-screen and you can even change your character colour!

173200.overview:
Published in Magic Disk 64 1994/06.

 A decent enough puzzle game in which you have to remove all the four-balled things by moving them into pillars. In a different time, in a different place: The Orbs live on a gigantic space station in a distant solar system called Theta Boroni, very close to the well-known Altair. There are four inhabited worlds in this system:

1. the mining planet Auron,
2. the farm planet Hestia,
3. the ocean planets Hydron and
4. the high-tech planet Argonia.

The orbs are very talented transport engineers, and they have therefore been hired with their space station to ensure the distribution of the goods to the individual planets. It was precisely for this purpose that the Orbs developed the large-capacity container, which consists of five spheres.
These are connected to one another: a small control and drive ball in the middle and four large balls on the outside, which contain the cargo space.
In addition, the orbs have invented special transmitters that pick up the containers and set them down on the correct planet. Each planet has been assigned a color so that there can be no mix-ups.

For example, the goods for Hestia arrive in green containers and are only transmitted to Hestia through the green-colored transmitter fields. Red stands for auron, gray for argonia and blue for hydron. If a transmitter field is reached by a large-capacity container of the same color that is moving towards it, it emits it and then closes again. It is completely irrelevant from which side the container approaches, since the transmitter field is so strong that it also works through its boundaries.

It is only necessary that the container is already moving towards it at a certain speed and is not located directly next to the transmitter field when it is heading towards it.

Of course, the orbs also have problems to contend with. First of all, there is inertia. Such a heavy large-capacity container, when it is in motion, can only be slowed with so much energy that the orbs have not even bothered to integrate brakes. Instead, they use high-density walls and simply let the containers made of special steel collide against them. If a container is not supposed to go in a certain direction, the orbs incorporate rebound elements. These send the containers back in the direction from which they came.
To make things easier, the orbs have also built in rotating segments that deflect the containers that are heading for them in the direction of the arrows.

173219.overview: You are in the Chamber of Light, in the Palace of King Elrad the Second. The room is very bright but you can see clearly. In the middle of the room is a Light crystal in the form of a cage which one held the orb of light but is now empty. You must restore the Orb of Light or darkness will rule the land.

173221.overview: A tile Removal brain game published in both Game On 1990/06, and Game On GE 1991/2. Space-themed Mahjong style game with some ace music by Rudolf Stember.

173222.overview: A Lander style game published in the "Cassette 50" collection. You are the pilot of a spacecraft in a fast decaying orbit above a giant planet covered in crevasses & deep fissures. You must pick a landing spot and have a go before your fuel runs out. Unfortunately for you the planet has a very strong gravity making landings at a safe speed extremely difficult.

173223.overview: A difficult avoid it style game with good music. With your spaceship you have got into the star system of Orion, in which you have now been held captive. In order to escape from the star system again, you have to collect a total of 18 energy bundles in the star system. An exciting action game with a lot of variety. You have been trapped in the solar system "Orion" with your space ship. To escape from there you have to find and collect 18 energy pills. A thrilling action game with plenty of variety.

173227.overview: Published in "BASIC Computer Games - Microcomputer Edition". Orbit challenges you to visualize spatial positions in polar coordinates. The object is to detonate a Photon explosive within a certain distance of a germ laden Romulan spaceship. This ship is orbiting a planet at a constant altitude and orbital rate (degrees/hour). The location of the ship is hidden by a cloaking device, but after each bomb you can determine how close to the enemy ship it exploded. The challenge is to hit an invisible moving target with a limited number of shots.

173228.overview: Orbit is a simple shooting game in which a spaceship is orbiting a planet. The player must fire a bomb. The player must specify the angle to fire the bomb at and the distance at which to make it explode. After firing the player either destroyed the ship and the game is over or the distance between the ship and the explosion is displayed and the player can try again for a new ship.

173229.overview: From the book "Commodore 64 GameMaster". You are in orbit around the planet Xeron. Your task is to flatten the buildings, and the beat off enemy fighters.

173230.overview: A shoot'em up created by Andrew S. Pakerski and published in both Loadstar #014, and later in Best of Loadstar #2. Have you ever wanted to shoot down enemy fighters like Luke Skywalker? If you have, then Orbit is for you. Orbit is a fast-paced game where you're flying through the vast emptiness of deep space and are attacked by fighters. your only choice is to fight to the death. The high-res background is your battlefield. On your control panel is a gauge the records the amount of damage you have sustained. When the gauge reaches 100%, it's lights out!! Fire when the enemy is within the crosshairs. You can even destroy his shots before they reach your ship.

173231.overview:
Published in Magic Disk 64 1994/11. 

This is another clone of the classic Tetris. The rules have been modified. The player's task is to prevent the well from filling up by combining blocks of the same color and pattern. The player must stack the blocks until the number on the information panel drops to zero. Points are deducted for the number of blocks falling and blocks removed from the well.

173232.overview:
A Logic\Brain game created by Marc Schubert and published in Magic Disk 64 1993/06. 

This is neither a computerized version of the cult science fiction series from the 1960s, nor an action-packed shooting game. "Orion" is a genuine thinking and puzzle game that is particularly impressive due to its simple gameplay. Attention!

Addictive! The playing field is divided into two parts. On the right there is a matrix that contains several stones. Each stone is given a number so that the task should now be clear. You must try with great skill to transfer the diagram shown on the right to the left side.
If you place a stone, all stones left and right next to it, above and below it are increased by the value one. In this way, the specified matrix can be reproduced.

At first everything is quite simple, but at higher levels the time limit gets tighter and hectic joystick rowing is often the result. Tip: Always stay relaxed!

After every 10. Level you will receive a password that you can use again in the next game so that you don't have to start all over again. If you have reached a high enough score to get into the highscore list, you can of course save it.

173240.overview: A 2D Adventure RPG published in Golden Disk 64 1993/01. The game is set in 1227 in the land of Beryland. The Ormus Cult has taken over the realm, and the PC has decided to do something about it. Character creation is just a name, at which point the player starts on "the southwest shores of Beryland," next to a city called Remfield. In addition to running around the land as a typical RPG character, you can hire troops and equip them. Troops are alternatives to regular combat--you can send them to fight wandering orcs and snakes and such--but they're mandatory for combats in which you try to seize or defend a city. Occasionally, as you explore, you come across a city that's "++OCCUPIED++" by the Ormus Cult, and to get in and take advantage of its services, you need to take the city.

173241.overview: The Ormus saga looks very similar to the early parts of the Ultima series. You live in Barryland, which has been taken over by the Ormus cult and now you have decided to do something about it. The quest starts near the city of Remfield at the southwest shores of Berryland. You can create your own character or simply start with the premade one and when you start the game you will be near a hostile town. You have very limited troops available at the start so attacking at this time is of no use. Around the world are treasures you can find to finance more troops and there are other places of interest as well like temples, castles and villages to visit. Along the way you will face monsters you can fight for experience and gold. The ultimate goal is to destroy the Ormus cult in their stronghold. The controls are keyboard based and doing things like entering a town and besieging are done using a menu system. The Ormus saga differs from other RPG's, as it also contains troop battles during a siege of a town or castle.

173242.overview: Ormus Saga III is the the final part of the Ormus saga trilogy. It takes the player back to Beryland, where numerous adventurers have to be ordered. Perfect for newcomers since you don't have to know either of the two predecessors!

173245.overview: Osar II is a single screen shooting game, where the player must hit the alien creature with a laser beam, while avoiding enemy attacks. Double enemy laser hit in the same ground spot damages the surface and form a hole. The hole is limiting the movement area, as contact with it means a loss of life.

173247.overview:
A scrolling screen platformer published in 64'er Sonderheft 79, 64'er 1999/05, SYS PD Diskett#49 (1994). After the failure of the nuclear reactor
are the insects around have mutated into monsters: killer wasps and cockroaches are the size of cow and they are grabbing up the residents of a small town in New Arizona. Everything flees. Only the farmer Oskar stands between them and those who must flee. Despite fierce resistance from the Spider-City citizens' initiative, the outdated nuclear power plant outside the city gates was not shut down. It happened as it had to happen: During an incident, radioactive waste water escaped and flowed into the Apache River. This was the beginning of the horror in Spider-City: wasps, spiders and beetles mutated into huge monsters due to the uncontrolled radioactivity and attacked people. 

Only one has the courage to take action against the beasts: Oskar, a farmer from the eastern edge of town. Armed with a lethal injection containing so much highly concentrated "DDT 5000" that one could use it to wipe out all the inhabitants of Spider-City in one fell swoop, he goes in search of the nuclear monsters. Help Oskar win the day.

173249.overview:
A parody of competition games like Winter Games and Track & Field where competitors challenge each other in cow milking and fishing skills. Created by Markus Faber and published in Golden Disk 64 1993/05. 
 
An obvious send-up of California Games, this is another humorous collection of competitive sporting events with a certain "local" character - this time set in Ostfriesland, Germany, where the collective taste in sports is apparently rather quaint. Popular regional games include cow milking (in which other cow products may be tossed into your opponent's bucket), shooting pigs (out of the sky), bike riding (with square wheels), teabag throwing, and (for that adrenaline-pumping extreme sports kick) competitive roof-building.

The above events blend playing against the clock, against the computer, and against another human player; you may practice each one individually or, if particularly lacking in self-respect, play the full set in a row. As with Blood 'n Guts, be ready for a lot of joystick waggling.

173267.overview: Based on the original 1978 code for the PET, this simple implementation for two players for the C64 was written by James Mendenhall and released for CBM machines based on early C64 development info this program would be ready for the C64 when it debuted.

173268.overview: Oubliette is one of the earliest party-based role-playing games. It is an open-ended hack-and-slash through a multilevel dungeon with a party of 1-6 characters, chosen from possible classes including Fighters, Priests and Thieves. They will gain experience, jewelry and armor as the adventure progresses, but they will also age and may eventually die. Spells are triggered through typing their activation codes. The party can be changed before every trip to the dungeon by dropping off / picking up characters from the local tavern.

173269.overview:
Othello/Reversi variation released by Wicket Software, a faithful simulation of a board game made already famous in the Renaissance and played by the princes of the time. The rules are simple: you change the color of the pieces that are in the middle of two others of opposite color. The object of the game is to fill the board with the largest number of pieces of your color. The adversary, very fierce, will be your beloved computer itself. Select the difficulty level ant the beginning of the game. Remember that the strategic points are the corners and the sides of the board, but you can only occupy them if your opponent has placed pieces in the rows bordering the edge. 

Published in Italy in the Play on tape Nuova serie - Super Games compilation tape.

173270.overview: A simple version of the classic board game, Othello that was published as part of "Leisure Time Classics" game pack.

173271.overview: A single player Othello game by Roger Svensson published by  Computer Boss International (CBI) of Sweden in 1988.

173272.overview: A very nice and aesthetically pleasing Othello game for one or two players created by Rickard Falk & Anders Pettersson with music by Drutten.

173274.overview: The game is a flick screen platformer, which has a very similar look and feel to Thing on a Spring, but with a bouncing Amiga red/white ball as the main character. Things are split across 6 levels in total, including themes such as Kitchen, Toys and Plants. You essentially have to switch off a load of switches on each level, to open a door at the end of the map to escape. In your way are a number of platforms, conveyor belts and creatures trying to stop you. You get one life and large block of energy to play with, which means the game is pretty tough.

173275.overview: A 2 player only dueling game created by Richard Bayliss & Hiram Kümper and released in 2000 by TND.

173276.overview: OUT is a Breakout style game developed by Axel Teichmann and published in Game On 1989/03.

173319.overview:
Published in both Happy Computer 1988/10, in 64'er Sonderheft 61 and 64'er Spielesammlung #4. 

In this vertically scrolling space shooter, dodge the diamond shaped ship of doom and zap the heck out of everything else.

173324.overview: A 2 Player only wild west duel across the cactus strewn desert of the west.

173325.overview:
A western themed shoot'em up included as one of the samples of the Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit. The adventure is set in the old Far West at the time of pioneers and sees two unscrupulous outlaws as protagonists. These bandits have to find safety by escaping to Mexico and to reach it they have to go through many areas full of dangers. These dangers are represented by the Native Americans of their territory, by the inhabitants of a town on the border of Arizona, by soldiers hunting for bandits by animals such as snakes, bison, etc. and by natural phenomena such as the winds and elements. To survive, our friends must carefully avoid the various bullets thrown at them, the animals and objects that the wind tosses in the duo's direction. To defend themselves from enemies, they can shoot with their trusty Colt sidearms. If you have a friend you can play both characters on the screen at the same time. 
 
While this was included in the Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit, it was released as a standalone game in Italy as Gina e Paolo in Special C64 n.3 (1991/1992) and as Attacco al Treno in COM 64 n.61 (gennaio/febbraio 1993).

173326.overview:
Out-Space is a Galaxianesque style shooter, albeit with strange enemies like umbrellas, slices of toast, fish, snakes and ladders, etc.

it was developed by Jason Tinkler in 2011 and released at Replay Expo 2011.

173328.overview: Overtake is a racing game that was part of the rather infamous Cassette 50 (think Action 52 for 8-bit Computers)

174280.overview:
Operation Metalstorm, designed by Alf Yngve with music and additional coding by Richard Bayliss, is a tribute to the 90s arcade game Terminator 2: Judgement Day and features plenty of robot blasting action.
 
The backstory to Operation Metalstorm is that us naive humans thought we could create an intelligent Robot population that would look after all of our needs, creating a world paradise with no war or poverty. Well, unfortunately the Robots don’t believe in the notion of ‘make love not war’ and have banded together with the aim of wiping out human civilisation.

Now its up to you, the best of the best, to stop them by finding the master computer and destroy it into smithereens. The World’s fate lies in your hands. Published in Reset 64 #11 and on the Reset #11 Mix-i-Disk.

176427.overview: Gábor Csendes envisions what Space Invaders would be like if it had had bosses. Released by ArtGame in 1996.

177952.overview: Outpost is a well-made clone of the Atari arcade classic Missile Command. It was developed by Thomas J. Czarnecki and published by Softdisk Publishing, Inc. in the North American based disk magazine Loadstar. It was published in both Loadstar #60, and Loadstar #193.

179493.overview:
A cross between Pong and air-hockey, a 2-player only head to head game. In a small arena with molybdenum walls, two players with nerves of steel will have to volley with a titanium sphere at constant acceleration using to gravito-magnetic repulsors that will be able to move in a limited area of the playing field. The aim being not only to protect one's own goal,  but to score the greatest number of goals on your opponent. Since the sphere will move faster and faster and with sometimes unpredictable direction, be very careful not to score on your own self!

Published in Italy as Old Game in both Hit Parade C64 n.19 (Gennaio 1988) and in Special Program n.37 (novembre 1987).

180278.overview: Osakesäästäjät is a Finnish language stock market simulation that can be played with up to 255 friends!!

180432.overview: in this table fire off your pinball and enter the Octagon! Created with the Pinball Construction Kit.

180435.overview:
The program simulates a trip over the Oregon Trail from Independence, Missouri, to Oregon City, Oregon, in the year 1847. Your family will cover the 2040 mile Oregon Trail in 5-6 months if you make it alive. You have saved $900, a small fortune, to spend for the trip and you've just paid $200 for a dependable wagon. You will need to spend the rest of your money on items that can help you make it alive to the end of the trail: Oxen, food, ammunition, clothing and miscellaneous supplies to treat sickness and for emergency repairs. 

So here is a great port of the version 2 source material (Creative Computing 1978-05) to the Commodore 64 computer.  Almost identical in display layout (if not colors) to a similar Atari 8-bit port.

Although it still closely hews to the source listing, being a BASIC implementation, the programmers for this version decided to try improvements to the status page that occurs after each turn.  Very nice.

180544.overview: Another fun pinball table created by the venerable CMD and published in the PCS Club Disk #01 and also in Stonysoft #1724.

180545.overview: A pinball table intended to make you smile and the follow up to the original Oddball table. This one was published in PCS Club Disk #14.

181153.overview:
A triple-combination slot machine simulator that is a hybrid fruit machine\card game with a scantily clad girl thrown in for prurient interest.  
 
Published in Italy under the name One-Arm Bandit in Videoteca Computer n.4.

181744.overview: You must find the clues and hidden items that will help you gain access to the chamber of the evil overlord, B'aalcknyte and defeat him to find your friends and win the game.

182287.overview:
Inspired by Wordzap, your purpose is to arrange words from the initial random letters. Unlike Wordzap which is a 2-player oriented game, you play against the clock to get the highest possible score. Your task is to arrange as many words as possible before the time runs out.

Features:

* 3 modes of play. EasyZap: You can choose freely from any of the letters. WordZap: You can only choose letters adjacent to an open square. BagoZap: You can choose letters near the last one selected (also diagonally).
* Dictionaries in 3 languages: English, Norwegian and German.
* High score saving, each game mode has a top 50 high score list, including date of achievement.

184652.overview: One could also be known as Uno, a video game much like the tabletop card game. It was published in Loadstar #019.

188859.overview:
A 3D maze shooter also released in Digital Marketing PD #021. You find yourself armed with a laser rifle inside of an insidious maze. You have to try to snare the little green monsters and then kill them. The more you move, the more you consume energy. Careful not to completely exhaust it, otherwise the game will be finished. Stopping too long in one place puts you at risk for attack to be on guard. 

Published in Italy as Obiettivo Alieni in Logica 2000 n.27 (Maggio 1986).

190902.overview: This is a fun little strategy game programmed by Matteo Angelini, using CC65 and C language. Othello Revenge is based on the all time classic board game, Reversi/Othello. This game features scrolling background graphics and presentation based using the charset from the Hanoi Tower, which Matteo launched a few months back. The idea of this game is to place as many pieces on to the board adjacent to your opponent, trying to capture as many of your opponent's pieces and transforming them to your own colour. This game consists of 4 different skill levels. One of which you can play against a friend or family member and another where you play against the computer. The harder the level the longer thinking time the computer has. At the end of the game, the winner will be decided when the game board is full or there are no possible moves.

192426.overview:
A shoot'em up, space invaders style game that was released as Odissea in Go Games n.8 (Aprile 1986). 
 
During an intergalactic journey flying your spaceship, you find yourself crossing an area dotted with asteroids that could damage your craft. To defend yourself, you must use your laser cannon to destroy them and thus clear your path. This mission will require all your reflexes, if you have any!

194614.overview: An undersea game released as part of the "C64/128 Battle Pack". Escape the grasping tentacles!

196126.overview:
In the tradition of "Hawkeye", you are steering a hero through a number of platform levels. In a shop you can obtain different weapons. Outrage inspires through colorful graphics and great design.

Outrage was produced by Cosmos Designs for the Boeder Talent Competition in cooperation with the 64'er magazine a long time ago. However, it was not released back then. We in Protovision bought the rights to distribute the game from Bernd Buchegger, who supplied us with the remnants of the game – of course without source codes and with a few bugs and glitches we'd liked to get fixed before a release. However, we were lacking the resources to work on this game, so we were looking for help. Psytronik came along and showed interest in finalizing and distributing the game, but they, too, were facing the same problems as we did. Thanks to everyone involved in this project, we can finally announce that Outrage has been completed!


Features:

-     5 levels fully packed with finest arcade action (Hawkeye style)
-     Each level with a monstrous end boss
-     A shop to buy ammunition, smartbombs and more
-     Colorful graphics, animations and special effects
-     Beautifully crafted SID in-game music and sfx
-     Title picture from STE'86 (Steve Day)
-     PAL and NTSC compatible

199031.overview:
You play "Old Sam" a hard working man who specializes in building and repairing bridges. Your goal is to take the pieces from the left side of the screen one by one and finish building the bridge to cross over to the castle. However, it's not as simple as it sounds as giant rocks are falling from the sky, and you must finish the bridge before either 1. the time runs out or 2. You lose all your lives by getting crushed to death by the boulders.

This game was developed by Roland Kunz and released by BB Software. The actual release year is not currently known.

199307.overview: The object of the game is to have the greatest number of tokens of your color at the end of the game. Published in French language Hebdogiciel N°007 (25.11.1983), and in Hebdogiciel Software N°1.

199398.overview: Interesting multigenre effort similar to Impossible Mission. Released in 1989 by Markt & Technik and made by Gordon Machel. You are on a spaceship to negotiate peace. The entire crew is kidnapped during a repair. Also published in Power-Games (Bestell-Nr. 38765).

200837.overview:
Operation Frog is an educational title where players explore the inner body of a frog. You can choose between a male and female frog in the References section. 

There are two game modes: Dissect and Reconstruct. 
In Dissect mode, players have to cut open the frog's body and remove its organs; and in Reconstruct mode, players have to put the already removed organs back to the frog's body in the correct order. 

This game offers you scissors, a probe, a magnifying glass and tweezers - the necessary tools for your work. The scissors help you cut the frog's body and remove organs, the probe gives you hints of where to cut  or which part to place first , the magnifying glass gives you information about each organ, and the tweezers help you move the organs.

The game offers players a saving function.

205667.overview: You play as a little explorers in a towers full of deadly traps and ugly batz. Your only weapons to help you win: quick-thinking and skill. It is a platforming game for one person, created by retrosouls and released in 2020.

205719.overview: The Outer Reaches is a science fiction themed pinball game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by J.P. using Olaf Lubeck's Pinball Construction Set in 1991. It was released as part of PCS Club Disk #28.

207445.overview: On the Grid is a single player snake game developed by Digital Monastery and released into the public domain on December 28, 2020.

207446.overview: A challenging 2D platformer from AnninaGames and Digital Monastery, released in 2019 as part of the RGCD 2019 Compo.

209293.overview:
Omnibus is a Polish language adaptation of a Hangman game. Being trapped in a locked room the player must find a password before the time runs out. With time expiring, each mistakenly indicated letter causes the lowering of the ceiling quicker. Guessing the password opens the door to the next level. The player can choose both consonants and vowels.

Unofficial English and Slovakian translations were released the same year.

210360.overview: A multi-event sports game created by Martin Kristensen and Søren Lund and released at the Commodore 64 Crap Game Compo 2004 (C64CGC), and later in GO64! 2004/07.

210589.overview: A one or two player SEUCK based shoot'em up including cooperative play created by Silvio Frattini (SilFrat)  and released in Italy in Commodore 64 Club #11 in 1989. Despite our precautions, what man feared for a long time has happened, we don't know how a terminal atomic war broke out, erasing mankind from the face of the planet. Over time some of the remaining beings did have evolved and birds seem to have taken the upper hand, perhaps by virtue of the intelligence developed on the others. But even for them to survive is not easy, on the planet there are in fact androids, mutant animals who, enraged by the events that have occurred, take it out on everything that is different from them. But you will have to try to survive at any cost if you don't want the Earth to go back millennia and therefore struggle strenuously to survive their deadly attacks and reach safety in the open.

210591.overview: A platformer game created by George Allan and published in both Commodore Disk User 1989/11, and in Your Commodore 1990/11 (Tape #10). Collect the numbers in this unusual arcade style adventure. You are trapped inside a base on an abstract world known as 'Orsital'. Your objective is to escape this unfriendly environment. You start at the base exit (that seems logical) which must be unlocked by collecting the numbers I to 9. These numbers are scattered about the base in no particular order. Once you have collected all nine numbers, you make your way back to the exit which will now be opened, thus enabling you to escape to the outside world. This is no easy feat, because the numbers must be collected in ascending order. It is advisable to search out and locate just where the numbers are before you start collecting them.

211253.overview: An arcade style Lander game created by RunStop64 and published as a preview in 2022. Rescue your stranded crew mates and return them to base before fuel runs out. Destroy the turret before it destroys you and your crew. WSAD keyboard controls.

211354.overview:
The Odyssey (not to be confused with the 1986 text adventure of the same game) is a 1984 public domain single player beat 'em up for the Commodore 64. 

It was the very first game developed by Stavros Fasoulas. If that name sounds familiar, it's because after this, he went on to code the C64 classics Delta, Quedex, and Sanxion for Thalamus.

213285.overview: An unpublished shooter from Narciso Quintana that was to be published by Dinamic Software, except, as he was underage, his parents would not sign off on the contract. The game was by Narisco but the graphics were property of Dinamic so the game could not be finished.  it only ever got as far as a simple test demo, with a score panel, enemies and a looping map. So enjoy a glimpse of a Dinamic game that never was.

213705.overview: Operation Brown Trousers is a 1-2 player (co-op) shooter for the C64. It was developed by Carlo Wijjy Wejszko and released into the public domain in 1989.

214116.overview:
Octopus-Adventure is a German language game in which you play Andover in a quest for gold. Your goal is to retrieve the gold from the bottom of the sea and return it to your boat. However fish, and a giant octopus are in your way. Catch and return the gold before the fish or Octopus tentacles catch you.

The game was developed by Michael Wellenhofer and published in CPU 1984/06.

216384.overview: A scrolling screen Argentinian platformer in both Spanish and English, created by Marcos J. Leguizamon and released in 1989. There are 29 levels to enjoy and be frustrated by.

216386.overview: A SEUCK based single player shooter created by Shaun Pearson in 1989.

216387.overview: A maze shooter, created by John Fedor and released in the Just for Fun compilation from Loadstar. Your escape begins by jumping off of a chopper. Your first objective is to collect the 5 energy cells and enter the complex. Shooting the robots will temporarily destroy them. The tank, however, is indestructible. Good luck!

216388.overview:
The fast-paced bean-juggling puzzle gameplay of the SEGA Megadrive games Puyo Puyo 2 / Dr Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine comes to the C64 for the first time.


Connect four or more beans of the same colour to clear them from the grid. Set up elaborate combos to send rocks to your opponents' side and ruin their carefully laid plans, or to avert rocks about to drop on yours! If your third column from the next fills up to the top, you lose.

219874.overview:
The Old West World a Game for the C64Maxi/Mini or a Real C64 and of course a Good C64 Emulator (Vice, Etc).
1 Player Push Scroll Left shoot em up, Shoot the Baddies but save the Lady's by walking into Them.
Made with the side ways Shoot 'Em' Up Construction Kit by Sensible Software and Jon Wells, Also V3 SEUCK Framework by Richard Bayliss.

219973.overview: An action game created by Betty Schueler, Gerald Schueler and published in Commodore Power/Play Vol.2 N.2 (Summer 1983).

239304.overview: Operation Merkur or Operation Mercury is a strategy game about the Battle of Crete a major Axis airborne and amphibious operation during World War II. It can be played trying for either Allied or German supremacy. Thanks to detailed maps, informative menus and extensive instructions, the overview of what is happening is maintained at all times. Many adjustable and special options and various re-loadable ones. Scenarios allow the degree of difficulty to vary. It was published in Golden Disk 64 1991/08.

417554.overview: Four oil companies (each of which can he human or computer controlled) do battle to dominate the lucrative oil industry, buying and selling oilfields around the world. You can choose one of four main goals, from topping the market in 3 years to total domination. Plenty of dirty tricks to help you are on offer, from setting fire to opponent's rigs to stealing the storage tanks which hold the oil in place. Private investigators can be hired to either prevent to prove these things. Although primarily a strategy game, a few short action sequences are also included. These come into play when attempting to drill for oil (you can hire a specialist to do this instead, but the cost is prohibitive in the early stages), to build oil pipelines around those of your opponents, and to extinguish any fires opponents start on your rig.

417636.overview:
Game created by Penny DeGroff and published in ReRun Special Summer Edition 1990. 

OUT OF ORDER is a great game for learning to alphabetize letters or for just having fun. All it takes is a little imagination! The scenario: You've just obtained a part-time position with the ABC Letter Car- riers Association. Your job: to quickly arrange, in alphabetical order, seven random letters and earn money in the process.

The game screen shows a six-by-seven matrix of squares, with seven letters in the bottom row and a "guard" moving back and forth in each of rows 2 through 5. The letter carrier starts on row 2 and places the alphabetized letters on the top row.
Suppose the letters at the bottom are N, C, T, Z, D, E and P. With a joystick in port 2, move the letter carrier to the square direcdy above the C (the first letter alphabetically) and press the firebutton; the C disappears. Then move the carrier to the first square in the second row, press the firebutton again, and the C appears direcdy above in row 1. Repeat this procedure until all the letters are in their correct alphabetical positions in the first row.
Of course, you don't have all day to do this! You must complete the alphabetizing task before a border, representing your work time so far, has been drawn around the screen.

The guards, continually moving back and forth in their rows, make the job more difficult. You can't move the letter carrier to a square occupied by a guard, and so must scoot around or wait for the guard to pass. Also, the guards won't hesitate to capture the carrier. When this happens at skill level 1 (the easiest), you keep the letter but lose some time. At level 2, the letter returns to its original square at the bottom of the screen, and you must fetch it again. At level 3, the guard takes the letter and won't give it back! 

When you've placed all the letters in the top row, or when the border is completely drawn, the delivered letters appear in a separate screen display. A letter is in its correct position if there is a green pointer below it. Otherwise, the appropriate letter for that position is shown beneath a red pointer.

448655.overview:
"Oel" (Oil), also published vith various names such as "Dallas," "Oel Pompowacze," "Oel Pumple" and "Oel Pumper" in various public domain compilations, is a German multiplayer business sim that lets the players manage oil companies, making strategic decisions to expand their operations and increase profits.

The gameplay is primarily text-based, with players selecting actions from multiple-choice options. These actions include purchasing drilling companies, pumping companies, tanker truck firms, oil fields, drilling equipment, pumps, and tankers. Additional options involve engaging in sabotage, setting prices, and continuing operations.

Players must manage their finances carefully, as the game displays the available funds and the cost of each option. Strategic planning is crucial to outmaneuver competitors and build a successful oil empire. The objective is to become the leading oil tycoon by making optimal business decisions and effectively managing resources.
